title: Drama
summary: Features of drama (acts and scenes, dialogue, stage directions, monologue, soliloquy, aside), dramatic structure, tension and irony, and analysing an original one-act scene.

notes.text: A **drama** (play) is written to be **performed** on stage. The story is told almost entirely through **dialogue** and **action**. The writer is the **playwright**, and the written text is the **script**.

rows: An **act** is a major division of a play; acts are divided into **scenes**, often marked by a change of place or time
Instructions in italics or brackets about movement, tone, setting, lighting and sound
A long speech by one character to others on stage
A speech in which a character, alone on stage, reveals their private thoughts to the audience
A brief remark to the audience that the other characters on stage cannot hear
The list of characters at the start of the play
Objects used on stage, the scenery, and what the actors wear

items: **Climax**: the moment of greatest tension; the turning point.

notes.label: Dramatic irony
notes.text: Drama often uses **dramatic irony**: the audience knows something a character does not, which builds tension or humour.

notes.title: Scene from 'The Envelope' (an original one-act play written for FreeSheet)
notes.text:
[A small kitchen in Mthatha. Evening. MAMA NOMVULA (50s) sits at the table sorting bills. Her son SIPHO (17) enters, hiding an envelope behind his back.]

SIPHO: (too cheerfully) Evening, Ma! You look… wonderful tonight.
MAMA NOMVULA: (without looking up) What did you break?
SIPHO: Nothing! Can a son not compliment his mother?
MAMA NOMVULA: A son can. My son does not. (She looks up.) What is behind your back?
SIPHO: (aside, to the audience) She has eyes like a hawk. If she sees the university stamp, she'll know I applied without telling her.
(He hesitates, then places the envelope on the table.)
SIPHO: It came today. I haven't opened it.
MAMA NOMVULA: (picking it up slowly) University of Cape Town. (A long pause.) Cape Town is very far, Sipho. And very expensive.
SIPHO: I know. That's why I didn't tell you. I didn't want you to worry about the money before… before there was anything to worry about.
MAMA NOMVULA: (her voice softening) So you carried this worry alone. (She holds out the envelope.) Open it. We will worry together.
(SIPHO tears it open. He reads in silence. The lights dim slowly until only his face is lit.)

notes.title: Analysing the scene
notes.problem: Explain the purpose of Sipho's aside and the effect of the final stage direction.
steps: The aside reveals Sipho's thoughts only to the audience: he applied to university secretly and fears his mother's reaction. This creates **dramatic irony**, because we know what is in the envelope before Mama Nomvula does.
The final stage direction (the lights dim until only his face is lit) focuses all attention on Sipho and creates **suspense**: the audience must wait to discover whether he has been accepted.
notes.answer: The aside creates dramatic irony; the lighting builds suspense and ends the scene on a climax.

steps: The climax is the point of greatest tension.

questions.prompt: Why does Mama Nomvula ask 'What did you break?' What does this show about her?
questions.memo:
✓ Sipho is being unusually cheerful and complimentary, so she suspects he is hiding something (1)
✓ She knows her son well / is shrewd and has a dry sense of humour (1)

questions.prompt: Identify and explain the figure of speech in 'She has eyes like a hawk.'
questions.memo:
✓ Simile (1)
✓ His mother is very observant / notices everything, as a hawk has sharp eyesight (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how Mama Nomvula's attitude changes in the scene, with reference to her words.
questions.memo:
✓ At first she is suspicious and stern ('What did you break?') (1)
✓ then worried about the cost ('very far… very expensive') (1)
✓ finally loving and supportive ('We will worry together') (1)

questions.prompt: Why is the stage direction '(her voice softening)' important for an actor?
questions.memo:
✓ It tells the actor how to deliver the line (1)
✓ showing the audience that her attitude has changed from worry to tenderness (1)

questions.prompt: What theme(s) does the scene explore? Support your answer.
questions.memo:
✓ Theme, e.g. family love and support / ambition versus financial hardship / honesty in families (1)
✓✓ Evidence from the scene: Sipho's secret application to protect his mother; her decision to share the worry (2)
